page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-64GB is a cloud server instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor within the Cloud Native family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The configuration provisions 8 shared virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 64.0 GB of system RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes no integrated local storage and no dedicated GPU accelerators. Additionally, network provisioning provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-core throughput alongside restricted single-threaded capability. In stress-ng evaluations, the server scored 783.79 in single-core performance, placing in the lower 10 percent of recorded results, whereas multi-core execution reached 6240.61. Standard computational testing via Geekbench recorded 1908.0 for single-core and 9055.0 for multi-core performance, supported by an aggregate PassMark CPU score of 15614.34. Memory throughput shows performance penalties under heavy streaming operations; large-block uncached read speeds registered at 32.5 GB/sec and write speeds at 24.93 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads maintained 833.5 GB/sec. Redis in-memory key-value processing demonstrated steady capability, handling 11.88 million SET operations per second.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio delivers high memory density while utilizing shared CPU resources, making the configuration cost-efficient for memory-dependent tasks that do not demand dedicated hardware threads. Because local storage is not bundled, external storage volumes must be attached for data persistence. This profile matches workloads such as in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, asynchronous queue workers, and moderate batch data pipelines where overall memory capacity outweighs single-thread execution latency.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-64GB is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. The instance provisions 8 shared vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing an expansive 8.0 GB per core memory footprint without bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware. In computational evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate multi-core processing capability, posting a Geekbench multi-core score of 9055.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 15614.34, although single-core execution and uncached memory bandwidth fall toward the lower testing tiers. Redis operations reach 11.88 million SET operations per second, confirming solid utility for in-memory caching layers. Combining dense memory capacity with shared compute resources, this instance delivers a cost-conscious option for memory-dependent tasks, including distributed caching, batch data processing, staging environments, and backend queuing systems that do not depend on dedicated single-core throughput.
